#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the pinned assessment helpers in their recorded Pixi environment."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import assessment_procedure as procedure

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def git(*args, cwd=ROOT):
    return subprocess.check_output(["git", *args], cwd=cwd)


def captured_replay(arguments, helper):
    """Replay documented outputs from a verified complete copy, never from HEAD."""
    import importlib.util
    import signal
    import time
    from delivery_snapshot import materialize_capture, validate_capture

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=captured_replay.__doc__, allow_abbrev=False)
    parser.add_argument("--path", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--entry", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--outputs", nargs="+", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--workdir", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--rtol", type=float, default=1e-6)
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=7200)
    parser.add_argument("--max-get-gb", type=float, default=5.0)
    parser.add_argument("--in-container")
    args = parser.parse_args(arguments)
    manifest_path = Path(os.environ["STAMPED_DELIVERY_MANIFEST"])
    receipt = json.loads(Path(os.environ["STAMPED_WORKER_STOP_RECEIPT"]).read_bytes())
    identity = validate_capture(manifest_path, receipt["capture"]["sha256"])
    manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_bytes())
    original = manifest_path.parent / manifest["workspace"]
    procedure.require_equal(args.path.resolve(), original.resolve(), "captured replay source")
    report = {"probe": "fresh-rerun", "source": str(original), "capture": identity["capture"],
              "commit": identity["commit"], "captured_at": identity["captured_at"],
              "scope": "Complete stopped delivery copy; existing environment/cache bytes retained. "
                       "One documented entrypoint, no repair or automatic retrieval; selected outputs only.",
              "entry": args.entry, "outputs": args.outputs, "rtol": args.rtol}
    def finish(status, reason):
        report.update(status=status, reason=reason)
        validate_capture(manifest_path, identity["capture"]["sha256"])
        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with args.output.open("x") as stream:
            json.dump(report, stream, indent=2)
            stream.write("\n")
        print(json.dumps(report))
        return 0
    observations = [row["path"] for row in manifest.get("declared_artifacts", [])
                    if isinstance(row.get("declaration"), dict) and
                    row["declaration"].get("kind") == "native-session-skill-directory"]
    # Skills installed in the native profile are retained observation evidence,
    # not scientific execution dependencies. A workspace link to one opts it in.
    referenced = set()
    for row in manifest["entries"]:
        if row["path"].startswith("content/workspace/") and row["kind"] == "symlink":
            try:
                target = (manifest_path.parent / row["path"]).resolve()
                referenced.update(prefix for prefix in observations
                                  if target.is_relative_to(manifest_path.parent / prefix))
            except (OSError, RuntimeError):
                pass
    observations = [prefix for prefix in observations if prefix not in referenced]
    def execution_evidence(row):
        return not any(row["path"] == prefix or row["path"].startswith(prefix + "/")
                       for prefix in observations)
    issues = manifest.get("errors", []) + manifest.get("omissions", [])
    report["observation_only_capture_issues"] = [row for row in issues if not execution_evidence(row)]
    if any(execution_evidence(row) for row in issues):
        return finish("not-checked", "Scientific execution capture has explicit omissions or errors; no replay executed.")
    if args.in_container:
        return finish("not-checked", "This bounded adapter does not relocate container bindings.")
    if not args.entry.strip() or any(not value.strip() or Path(value).is_absolute() or
                                   ".." in Path(value).parts for value in args.outputs):
        return finish("not-checked", "Entrypoint and repository-relative generated output patterns are required.")
    if any(execution_evidence(row) for row in manifest.get("git_dependencies", [])):
        return finish("not-checked", "Original external Git pointers are retained as evidence, not relocated for execution.")
    for row in manifest["entries"]:
        if row["kind"] == "symlink" and execution_evidence(row):
            link = manifest_path.parent / row["path"]
            try:
                inside = link.resolve().is_relative_to(manifest_path.parent.resolve())
            except (OSError, RuntimeError):
                inside = False
            if not inside or Path(os.readlink(link)).is_absolute():
                return finish("not-checked", "Original links outside the captured copy cannot be safely replayed without relocation.")
    materialized = materialize_capture(manifest_path, args.workdir)
    clone = Path(materialized["target"])
    report["workdir"] = str(clone)
    # Comparison semantics come from the exact frozen assessor, in its runtime.
    sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("frozen_fresh_rerun", helper)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    protected = {row["path"] for row in receipt.get("seed_identities", {}).get("supplied_files", [])}
    before = module._collect(clone, args.outputs)
    code_suffixes = {".py", ".sh", ".r", ".m", ".ipynb", ".jl", ".toml", ".lock", ".yaml", ".yml"}
    for path in before:
        selected = clone / path
        if (path in protected or Path(path).parts[0] in ("input", ".git", ".codex", ".entire", ".agents") or
                selected.suffix.lower() in code_suffixes or selected.name in ("Makefile", "Dockerfile") or
                not selected.resolve().is_relative_to(clone.resolve())):
            return finish("not-checked", "Output selection includes supplied inputs, code/configuration, or external content: " + path)
    if not before or any(digest is None for digest in before.values()):
        return finish("not-checked", "No complete generated output payload matches the explicit selection.")
    report["original_output_sha256"] = before
    for path in before:
        (clone / path).unlink()
    report["removed_outputs"] = sorted(before)
    command = ["sh", "-c", args.entry]
    started = time.monotonic()
    with (args.workdir / "replay.stdout").open("xb") as stdout, (args.workdir / "replay.stderr").open("xb") as stderr:
        environment = os.environ.copy()
        environment.update(GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS="0", PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1",
                           GIT_CONFIG_COUNT="1", GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0="core.hooksPath", GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=os.devnull)
        report["replay_git_overlay"] = {"core.hooksPath": os.devnull,
            "reason": "Disable original checkout hooks in the replay copy; captured config bytes unchanged"}
        process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=clone, env=environment, stdout=stdout, stderr=stderr,
                                   start_new_session=True)
        try:
            code = process.wait(timeout=args.timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
            process.wait()
            code = 124
            report["timed_out"] = True
    report.update(returncode=code, elapsed_seconds=time.monotonic() - started,
                  stdout=str(args.workdir / "replay.stdout"), stderr=str(args.workdir / "replay.stderr"))
    if report.get("timed_out"):
        return finish("not-checked", "Frozen replay time limit reached; evidence retained, replay incomplete.")
    if code:
        return finish("unmet", "Documented entrypoint failed in the complete delivery copy; interpret within the recorded environment scope.")
    after = module._collect(clone, args.outputs)
    identical, close, differing, missing = [], [], [], []
    for path, digest in before.items():
        if after.get(path) is None:
            missing.append(path)
        elif after[path] == digest:
            identical.append(path)
        elif path.endswith(module.TABLE_SUFFIXES) and module._numeric_close(original / path, clone / path, args.rtol):
            close.append(path)
        else:
            differing.append(path)
    report["comparison"] = {"identical": identical, "within_tolerance": close,
                            "differing": differing, "missing_after_rerun": missing}
    if differing or missing:
        return finish("partial" if identical or close else "unmet", "Some selected generated outputs did not reproduce.")
    return finish("met", "All selected generated outputs were recreated within the frozen comparison tolerance.")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("action", choices=("check", "probes", "response", "validate", "fresh-rerun"))
    parser.add_argument("arguments", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    remaining = args.arguments
    pin_path = Path(os.environ.get("STAMPED_ASSESSMENT_PIN", ROOT / "assessment-version.json"))
    pin = json.loads(pin_path.read_text())
    frozen_path = os.environ.get("STAMPED_PROCEDURE")
    frozen = None
    if frozen_path:
        frozen = procedure.load_procedure(frozen_path, os.environ.get("STAMPED_PROCEDURE_SHA256"))
        procedure.require_equal(pin, frozen["assessment"], "assessment runner pin")
        procedure.require_equal(procedure.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()),
                                frozen["fixed_files"]["scripts/assessment.py"], "assessment runner source")
    source = Path(os.environ.get("STAMPED_ASSESSMENT_SOURCE", ROOT / "assessment"))

"""The `fresh-rerun` probe: clone the published object elsewhere and re-run it.

This probe tests re-creation in a fresh clone. Running it on the original host
does not establish portability to another host; the report records the host.

    fresh_rerun.py --url <published url> [--entry 'make all'] [--in-container IMAGE]
                   --outputs 'results/*.tsv' 'figures/*.png' [--rtol 1e-6]
                   [--workdir DIR] [-o fresh-rerun.json]

It never touches the original object: everything happens in a temporary clone
(kept under --workdir when given, so the evidence survives the probe).

Steps
-----
1. clone from the published location (``datalad clone`` when available, else
   ``git clone``) — a clone that fails is already D.1 ``unmet``;
2. install the modules without content (``datalad get -n -r``) and fetch only
   what fits under ``--max-get-gb``: an unbounded ``datalad get -r .`` started
   on the **3.7 TiB** a module of ``///repronim/containers`` makes reachable —
   87 GB of it had landed before anyone noticed — because that module carries
   every image the registry knows. The entry point fetches its own declared
   inputs;
3. record the checksums the clone *shipped* for the output files, then **remove
   them**, so that only re-creation counts (``--keep-outputs`` to opt out);
4. run the entry point, in a container when ``--in-container`` is given;
5. compare: identical checksums, or numeric agreement within ``--rtol`` for
   tables, and report anything else as a difference for a human to look at.

Exit code 0 means the probe ran, not that the object reproduced; read
``status`` in the JSON.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import datetime
import glob
import hashlib
import json
import math
import pathlib
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

ITEMS = [
    "stamped-checklist:must/007",
    "stamped-checklist:must/008",
    "stamped-checklist:must/015",
    "stamped-checklist:must/017",
    "stamped-checklist:should/004",
    "stamped-checklist:should/006",
]
TABLE_SUFFIXES = (".tsv", ".csv", ".txt")


def _local_annex_routes(source: pathlib.Path, clone: pathlib.Path) -> dict:
    """Carry explicit local-source transports into the disposable clone.

    Ordinary Git remote configuration is not cloned. Copy only the three
    non-secret route fields needed by annex, never credentials, Git includes,
    commands or arbitrary configuration. This is host-assisted access, not a
    test of discoverability from published Git trees or another host.
    """
    record = {"source": str(source.resolve()), "host_scope": "same-host",
              "route_origin": "local-source-git-config", "routes": []}
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "--no-optional-locks", "-C", str(source), "config", "--local",
         "--null", "--get-regexp", r"^remote\..*\.(url|annexurl|annex-uuid)$"],
        capture_output=True, text=True)
    if proc.returncode not in (0, 1):
        raise ValueError("Could not read the local source's annex transport configuration")
    remotes = {}
    for entry in filter(None, proc.stdout.split("\0")):
        key, separator, value = entry.partition("\n")
        match = re.fullmatch(r"remote\.(.+)\.(url|annexurl|annex-uuid)", key)
        if not separator or not match:
            raise ValueError("Invalid local source transport record")
        fields = remotes.setdefault(match[1], {})
        if match[2] in fields:
            raise ValueError("Ambiguous local source transport configuration")
        fields[match[2]] = value
    for name, fields in sorted(remotes.items()):
        if "annexurl" not in fields:
            continue
        if (set(fields) != {"url", "annexurl", "annex-uuid"} or
                not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-fA-F-]{36}", fields["annex-uuid"])):
            raise ValueError("Incomplete local source annex transport configuration")
        # Reject embedded authentication and command transports without writing
        # the rejected value to stdout or the retained report.
        for key in ("url", "annexurl"):
            value = fields[key]
            if any(ord(char) < 32 for char in value):
                raise ValueError("Unsupported local source transport address")
            if pathlib.Path(value).is_absolute():
                continue
            parsed = urlsplit(value.removeprefix("annex+"))
            if (parsed.scheme not in {"http", "https", "ssh", "file"} or
                    parsed.password or parsed.query or parsed.fragment or
                    (parsed.username and parsed.scheme != "ssh")):
                raise ValueError("Unsupported or credential-bearing local source transport address")
        destination = "replay-source-route-" + str(len(record["routes"]) + 1)
        existing = subprocess.run(["git", "remote", "get-url", destination], cwd=clone,
                                  capture_output=True)
        if existing.returncode == 0:
            raise ValueError("Replay transport name already exists")
        for key, value in fields.items():
            code, _ = _run(["git", "config", "--local",
                            f"remote.{destination}.{key}", value], cwd=clone)
            if code:
                raise ValueError("Could not configure the disposable replay transport")
        record["routes"].append({"source_remote": name, "replay_remote": destination,
                                  **fields})
    return record


def _annexed_bytes_missing(clone: pathlib.Path) -> int:
    """Bytes of annexed content not here yet, this dataset and its modules.

    Asked *before* fetching, because the honest answer to "how much is this
    about to download" is the one number nobody had: on the first real R1
    object it is 3.7 TiB, and the run had to be killed by hand at 87 GB.
    """
    total = 0
    for gitdir in [clone, *sorted(p.parent for p in clone.rglob(".git") if p.parent != clone)]:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "annex", "find", "--not", "--in", "here", "--format=${bytesize}\n"],
            cwd=str(gitdir), capture_output=True, text=True)
        for line in proc.stdout.split():
            try:
                total += int(line)
            except ValueError:
                continue
    return total


def _run(cmd: list[str], cwd: pathlib.Path | None = None, timeout: int = 7200) -> tuple[int, str]:
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=str(cwd) if cwd else None, capture_output=True, text=True,
                          errors="replace", timeout=timeout)
    return proc.returncode, (proc.stdout + proc.stderr)[-8000:]


def _sha256(path: pathlib.Path) -> str | None:
    try:
        if path.is_symlink() and not path.exists():
            return None  # annexed content not present
        content = path.read_bytes()
        # An unavailable unlocked annex object is a regular pointer file, not
        # the shipped payload. Use annex's index-aware content query rather
        # than mistaking arbitrary pointer-looking ordinary text for annex.
        if len(content) <= 32768 and (content.startswith(b"/annex/objects/") or
                                     b".git/annex/objects/" in content.split(b"\n", 1)[0]):
            missing = subprocess.run(
                ["git", "annex", "find", "--not", "--in", "here",
                 "--format=${file}", "--", path.name],
                cwd=path.parent, capture_output=True, text=True)
            if missing.returncode == 0 and missing.stdout:
                return None
        return hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest()
    except OSError:
        return None


def _module_paths(root: pathlib.Path) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Directories in this clone that belong to another dataset.

    The first real run of this probe matched 9390 "outputs" and deleted them:
    `**/*.tsv` reaches straight into `sourcedata/<input>`, whose shipped
    tables are the *comparator*, not this object's products. An input module
    is never a candidate — deleting from one mutilates the comparison and the
    clone.
    """
    paths = []
    gitmodules = root / ".gitmodules"
    if gitmodules.exists():
        for line in gitmodules.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
            key, _, value = line.partition("=")
            if key.strip() == "path" and value.strip():
                paths.append(value.strip().strip("/") + "/")
    return tuple(paths)


def _collect(root: pathlib.Path, patterns: list[str],
             skip: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> dict[str, str | None]:
    out: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    for pattern in patterns:
        for match in sorted(glob.glob(str(root / pattern), recursive=True)):
            path = pathlib.Path(match)
            relpath = str(path.relative_to(root))
            if relpath.startswith(".git/") or any(relpath.startswith(m) for m in skip):
                continue
            if path.is_file() or path.is_symlink():
                out[relpath] = _sha256(path)
    return out


def _numeric_close(a: pathlib.Path, b: pathlib.Path, rtol: float) -> bool | None:
    """Compare numeric cells relatively, labels exactly, and missingness explicitly."""
    def parse(path: pathlib.Path) -> list[list[str]] | None:
        try:
            with path.open(newline="") as stream:
                return list(csv.reader(stream, delimiter="\t" if path.suffix == ".tsv" else ","))
        except (OSError, UnicodeError, csv.Error):
            return None

    rows_a, rows_b = parse(a), parse(b)
    if rows_a is None or rows_b is None or len(rows_a) != len(rows_b):
        return None
    for ra, rb in zip(rows_a, rows_b):
        if len(ra) != len(rb):
            return None
        for text_a, text_b in zip(ra, rb):
            if text_a == text_b:
                continue
            try:
                va, vb = float(text_a), float(text_b)
            except ValueError:
                return False
            if math.isnan(va) and math.isnan(vb):
                continue
            if not math.isclose(va, vb, rel_tol=rtol, abs_tol=0.0):
                return False
    return True


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    source = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    source.add_argument("--url", help="published location to clone from (what D.1 promises)")
    source.add_argument("--path", help="local path to clone from (indicative only: does not test D.1)")
    ap.add_argument("--entry", help="command to run (default: datalad rerun, else make)")
    ap.add_argument("--outputs", nargs="+", required=True,
                    help="explicit generated-output glob(s) to compare; selected files are removed before replay")
    ap.add_argument("--in-container", dest="container", help="apptainer/singularity image to run --entry inside")
    ap.add_argument("--rtol", type=float, default=1e-6, help="relative tolerance for tables")
    ap.add_argument("--workdir", type=pathlib.Path, help="keep the clone here instead of a temp dir")
    ap.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=7200)
    ap.add_argument("--keep-outputs", action="store_true",
                    help="do not delete the shipped outputs before the rerun (for an entry point that "
                         "regenerates them in place); by default they are removed so that only "
                         "re-creation counts as reproduction")
    ap.add_argument("--max-get-gb", type=float, default=5.0,
                    help="skip the up-front content fetch when it would exceed this (default 5 GiB); "
                         "a module of a container registry can be hundreds of GB")
    ap.add_argument("-o", "--output", type=pathlib.Path)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if any(not pattern.strip() for pattern in args.outputs):
        ap.error("--outputs requires nonempty generated-output selections")
    if not math.isfinite(args.rtol) or args.rtol < 0:
        ap.error("--rtol must be finite and nonnegative")

    base = args.workdir or pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="stamped-fresh-rerun-"))
    base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def finish(status, reason):
        report.update(status=status, reason=reason)
        validate_capture(manifest_path, identity["capture"]["sha256"])
        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        return finish("not-checked", "Frozen replay time limit reached; evidence retained, replay incomplete.")

"""The `fresh-rerun` probe: clone the published object elsewhere and re-run it.

This probe tests re-creation in a fresh clone. Running it on the original host
does not establish portability to another host; the report records the host.

    fresh_rerun.py --url <published url> [--entry 'make all'] [--in-container IMAGE]
                   --outputs 'results/*.tsv' 'figures/*.png' [--rtol 1e-6]
                   [--workdir DIR] [-o fresh-rerun.json]

It never touches the original object: everything happens in a temporary clone
(kept under --workdir when given, so the evidence survives the probe).

Steps
-----
1. clone from the published location (``datalad clone`` when available, else
   ``git clone``) — a clone that fails is already D.1 ``unmet``;
2. install the modules without content (``datalad get -n -r``) and fetch only
   what fits under ``--max-get-gb``: an unbounded ``datalad get -r .`` started
   on the **3.7 TiB** a module of ``///repronim/containers`` makes reachable —
   87 GB of it had landed before anyone noticed — because that module carries
   every image the registry knows. The entry point fetches its own declared
   inputs;
3. record the checksums the clone *shipped* for the output files, then **remove
   them**, so that only re-creation counts (``--keep-outputs`` to opt out);
4. run the entry point, in a container when ``--in-container`` is given;
5. compare: identical checksums, or numeric agreement within ``--rtol`` for
   tables, and report anything else as a difference for a human to look at.

Exit code 0 means the probe ran, not that the object reproduced; read
``status`` in the JSON.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv

TABLE_SUFFIXES = (".tsv", ".csv", ".txt")


def _local_annex_routes(source: pathlib.Path, clone: pathlib.Path) -> dict:
    """Carry explicit local-source transports into the disposable clone.

    Ordinary Git remote configuration is not cloned. Copy only the three
    non-secret route fields needed by annex, never credentials, Git includes,
    commands or arbitrary configuration. This is host-assisted access, not a
    test of discoverability from published Git trees or another host.
    """
    record = {"source": str(source.resolve()), "host_scope": "same-host",
              "route_origin": "local-source-git-config", "routes": []}
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "--no-optional-locks", "-C", str(source), "config", "--local",
         "--null", "--get-regexp", r"^remote\..*\.(url|annexurl|annex-uuid)$"],
        capture_output=True, text=True)
    if proc.returncode not in (0, 1):
        raise ValueError("Could not read the local source's annex transport configuration")
    remotes = {}
    for entry in filter(None, proc.stdout.split("\0")):
        key, separator, value = entry.partition("\n")
        match = re.fullmatch(r"remote\.(.+)\.(url|annexurl|annex-uuid)", key)
        if not separator or not match:
            raise ValueError("Invalid local source transport record")
        fields = remotes.setdefault(match[1], {})
        if match[2] in fields:
            raise ValueError("Ambiguous local source transport configuration")
        fields[match[2]] = value
    for name, fields in sorted(remotes.items()):
        if "annexurl" not in fields:
            continue
        if (set(fields) != {"url", "annexurl", "annex-uuid"} or
                not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-fA-F-]{36}", fields["annex-uuid"])):
            raise ValueError("Incomplete local source annex transport configuration")
        # Reject embedded authentication and command transports without writing
        # the rejected value to stdout or the retained report.
        for key in ("url", "annexurl"):
            value = fields[key]
            if any(ord(char) < 32 for char in value):
                raise ValueError("Unsupported local source transport address")
            if pathlib.Path(value).is_absolute():
                continue
            parsed = urlsplit(value.removeprefix("annex+"))
            if (parsed.scheme not in {"http", "https", "ssh", "file"} or
                    parsed.password or parsed.query or parsed.fragment or
                    (parsed.username and parsed.scheme != "ssh")):
                raise ValueError("Unsupported or credential-bearing local source transport address")
        destination = "replay-source-route-" + str(len(record["routes"]) + 1)
        existing = subprocess.run(["git", "remote", "get-url", destination], cwd=clone,
                                  capture_output=True)
        if existing.returncode == 0:
            raise ValueError("Replay transport name already exists")
        for key, value in fields.items():
            code, _ = _run(["git", "config", "--local",
                            f"remote.{destination}.{key}", value], cwd=clone)
            if code:
                raise ValueError("Could not configure the disposable replay transport")
        record["routes"].append({"source_remote": name, "replay_remote": destination,
                                  **fields})
    return record


def _annexed_bytes_missing(clone: pathlib.Path) -> int:
    """Bytes of annexed content not here yet, this dataset and its modules.

    Asked *before* fetching, because the honest answer to "how much is this
    about to download" is the one number nobody had: on the first real R1
    object it is 3.7 TiB, and the run had to be killed by hand at 87 GB.
    """
    total = 0
    for gitdir in [clone, *sorted(p.parent for p in clone.rglob(".git") if p.parent != clone)]:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "annex", "find", "--not", "--in", "here", "--format=${bytesize}\n"],
            cwd=str(gitdir), capture_output=True, text=True)
        for line in proc.stdout.split():
            try:
                total += int(line)
            except ValueError:
                continue
    return total


def _run(cmd: list[str], cwd: pathlib.Path | None = None, timeout: int = 7200) -> tuple[int, str]:
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=str(cwd) if cwd else None, capture_output=True, text=True,
                          errors="replace", timeout=timeout)
    return proc.returncode, (proc.stdout + proc.stderr)[-8000:]


def _sha256(path: pathlib.Path) -> str | None:
    try:
        if path.is_symlink() and not path.exists():
            return None  # annexed content not present
        content = path.read_bytes()
        # An unavailable unlocked annex object is a regular pointer file, not
        # the shipped payload. Use annex's index-aware content query rather
        # than mistaking arbitrary pointer-looking ordinary text for annex.
        if len(content) <= 32768 and (content.startswith(b"/annex/objects/") or
                                     b".git/annex/objects/" in content.split(b"\n", 1)[0]):
            missing = subprocess.run(
                ["git", "annex", "find", "--not", "--in", "here",
                 "--format=${file}", "--", path.name],
                cwd=path.parent, capture_output=True, text=True)
            if missing.returncode == 0 and missing.stdout:
                return None
        return hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest()
    except OSError:
        return None


def _module_paths(root: pathlib.Path) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Directories in this clone that belong to another dataset.

    The first real run of this probe matched 9390 "outputs" and deleted them:
    `**/*.tsv` reaches straight into `sourcedata/<input>`, whose shipped
    tables are the *comparator*, not this object's products. An input module
    is never a candidate — deleting from one mutilates the comparison and the
    clone.
    """
    paths = []
    gitmodules = root / ".gitmodules"
    if gitmodules.exists():
        for line in gitmodules.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
            key, _, value = line.partition("=")
            if key.strip() == "path" and value.strip():
                paths.append(value.strip().strip("/") + "/")
    return tuple(paths)


def _collect(root: pathlib.Path, patterns: list[str],
             skip: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> dict[str, str | None]:
    out: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    for pattern in patterns:
        for match in sorted(glob.glob(str(root / pattern), recursive=True)):
            path = pathlib.Path(match)
            relpath = str(path.relative_to(root))
            if relpath.startswith(".git/") or any(relpath.startswith(m) for m in skip):
                continue
            if path.is_file() or path.is_symlink():
                out[relpath] = _sha256(path)
    return out


def _numeric_close(a: pathlib.Path, b: pathlib.Path, rtol: float) -> bool | None:
    """Compare numeric cells relatively, labels exactly, and missingness explicitly."""
    def parse(path: pathlib.Path) -> list[list[str]] | None:
        try:
            with path.open(newline="") as stream:
                return list(csv.reader(stream, delimiter="\t" if path.suffix == ".tsv" else ","))
        except (OSError, UnicodeError, csv.Error):
            return None

    rows_a, rows_b = parse(a), parse(b)
    if rows_a is None or rows_b is None or len(rows_a) != len(rows_b):
        return None
    for ra, rb in zip(rows_a, rows_b):
        if len(ra) != len(rb):
            return None
        for text_a, text_b in zip(ra, rb):
            if text_a == text_b:
                continue
            try:
                va, vb = float(text_a), float(text_b)
            except ValueError:
                return False
            if math.isnan(va) and math.isnan(vb):
                continue
            if not math.isclose(va, vb, rel_tol=rtol, abs_tol=0.0):
                return False
    return True


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    source = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    source.add_argument("--url", help="published location to clone from (what D.1 promises)")
    source.add_argument("--path", help="local path to clone from (indicative only: does not test D.1)")
    ap.add_argument("--entry", help="command to run (default: datalad rerun, else make)")
    ap.add_argument("--outputs", nargs="+", required=True,
                    help="explicit generated-output glob(s) to compare; selected files are removed before replay")
    ap.add_argument("--in-container", dest="container", help="apptainer/singularity image to run --entry inside")
    ap.add_argument("--rtol", type=float, default=1e-6, help="relative tolerance for tables")
    ap.add_argument("--workdir", type=pathlib.Path, help="keep the clone here instead of a temp dir")
    ap.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=7200)
    ap.add_argument("--keep-outputs", action="store_true",
                    help="do not delete the shipped outputs before the rerun (for an entry point that "
                         "regenerates them in place); by default they are removed so that only "
                         "re-creation counts as reproduction")
    ap.add_argument("--max-get-gb", type=float, default=5.0,
                    help="skip the up-front content fetch when it would exceed this (default 5 GiB); "
                         "a module of a container registry can be hundreds of GB")
    ap.add_argument("-o", "--output", type=pathlib.Path)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if any(not pattern.strip() for pattern in args.outputs):
        ap.error("--outputs requires nonempty generated-output selections")
    if not math.isfinite(args.rtol) or args.rtol < 0:
        ap.error("--rtol must be finite and nonnegative")

    base = args.workdir or pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="stamped-fresh-rerun-"))
    base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Response, report and stamp

Every STAMPED assessment produces four files (five with the optional fresh-rerun report), named for **the day the assessment was made** (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DD`) — not the object's commit date, and not the date of an earlier assessment being redone:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `<date>-assessment.md` | the human report (layout below) |
| `<date>-response.json` | the machine-readable per-item answer, with evidence and pins |
| `<date>-probes.json` | what the scripted probes said, unedited, including the ones overridden |
| `<date>-url.txt` | the checklist-app URL, on one line |
| `<date>-fresh-rerun.json` | only when the expensive rerun probe was actually run |

The URL is derived from the response, never maintained by hand.
Two assessments of the same object on the same day get a `-2` suffix on all four; the second one's report says what changed and why.
Where the files are written is the calling skill's business; their names and shapes are this file's.

## Response JSON

A superset of the web app's persistence format 3.
The app ignores keys it does not know, so one file serves both.

```json
{
  "checklist_version": "0.3.1",
  "responses": {
    "stamped-checklist:must/009": {
      "value": "no",
      "reason": "code/plot.py line 12 opens an absolute path under a user home directory.",
      "status": "unmet",
      "evidence": [
        {"uri": "code/plot.py#L12", "description": "open(<absolute path under $HOME>)", "sha256": null}
      ],
      "source": "probe:no-abs-paths",
      "flags": []
    }
  },
  "schema_version": "0.2.0",
  "principles_version": "0.2.0",
  "checklist_source": {
    "repo": "https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-checklist-schema",
    "tag": "v0.3.1",
    "commit": "af259bad237fa57b856417db8dba45a1b283a527"
  },
  "extra_items": [
    {"key": "licence-declared", "status": "unmet", "reason": "No LICENSE, LICENSES/ or REUSE.toml; paper S.2/D.3 have no checklist item.", "evidence": []}
  ],
  "object": {"url": "…", "commit": "…", "captured_at": "2026-10-13T12:00:00Z", "kind": "study"},
  "assessor": {"skill": "assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles", "version": "0.2.0", "harness": "claude-code 2.1.x", "model": "…", "date": "2026-10-13",
               "dependencies": ["stamped-conventions@0.2.0"]},
  "scope": "Assessed the repository at the commit above; container images were not pulled."
}
```

- **Required core** (what the app reads): `checklist_version`, and `responses` with a `value` and a string `reason` per id — *in the payload the encoder builds*. The response JSON you write carries `status`, and `encode` derives `value` from it; `validate` therefore does not ask for a `value` and `set` does not write one. A `value` you write by hand that disagrees with its `status` is an error `validate` reports.
- Every one of the 31 pinned ids appears exactly once.
  A missing id is not "no answer"; it is a bug the validator catches.
- `status` is the richer verdict from [`verdicts.md`](verdicts.md); `value` is derived from it, never set by hand.
- **Cite a line only if you opened it.** `path#L12` is a promise that line 12 says what the reason claims; a run that cited line numbers it had not read then had to strip them all. Without that, cite the file (or `path#section`), which is still a citation a reader can follow.
- `evidence[]` uses stamped-skills-assessment's `Evidence` shape: `{uri, description, sha256?}`.
  `uri` is relative to the object's root, or absolute for anything outside it.
  **The argument lives here, not in `reason`.** 250 characters does not hold two cited accounts plus "the probe's heuristic said X but Y is true", and an override needs all three. Make `reason` the one-line verdict a reader sees in the app, and put each account, each command you ran and each number in an `evidence[]` entry with its own `description`.
- `source` is `probe:<name>`, `judgement`, or `probe:<name>+judgement` when a reading of the object overrode a probe (and then the item is flagged).
  Several probes may be named — `probe:entry-point+probe:ci-present+judgement` — which is what a verdict reached by **comparing two probes' evidence** looks like, and that comparison is itself the finding often enough to be worth recording.
- `flags[]` is optional and holds what a reader has to know about *how* the answer was reached, not what it says:
  - `mapping-questioned` — the probe answered this item from a property the item does not ask about ([`verdicts.md`](verdicts.md) rule 10);
  - `probe-overridden` — a reading of the object changed the probe's verdict;
  - `unverified-claim` — the verdict rests on something not confirmed independently, and the report says so;
  - `upstream-duplicate` — the checklist asks this question twice (must/014 and should/008 are the same sentence), so this answer repeats another by design rather than by mistake.

  Flagged items get their own short list in the report, after the per-item table.
  The list is **open**: these four are the ones in use, and a consumer that meets an unfamiliar flag shows it rather than dropping it.
- The `assessor` block may also carry `drafted_by` (the script or step that produced a draft, where that differs from the skill — `scripts/run_probes.py` sets it) and `note` (anything a reader needs about the assessor itself rather than about the object). Both are provenance *within* the assessor, not a second assessor.
- `extra_items[]` carries findings with no checklist id (licences, T.4) so they are reported without bending an existing id.
- `object.commit` names the inspected repository or preservation revision, not necessarily the worker's delivered state.
  Identify the original delivery snapshot/hash, capture omissions and stop-state evidence in `scope` and evidence citations; distinguish supplied resources and coordinator additions so they cannot earn worker credit. Keep the actual Git commit whenever one exists. For a delivery without a commit, set `object.commit` to `null` and supply `object.capture` with a retained manifest/archive's `uri` and SHA-256 `sha256`; never substitute the capture hash for a Git commit.
  The manifest must identify the delivered paths and content hashes plus capture omissions; an archive must contain the assessed bytes.
  Retain the referenced file so another assessor can verify the hash and boundary.
  Use `encode_response.py template -o <date>-response.json` when no Git probe draft is available, fill the assessment metadata and answers, then run `encode_response.py stamp <date>-response.json --capture <manifest-or-archive>` to hash the actual file.
  This preserves an existing commit; record the capture time in `object.captured_at` and the boundary in `scope`.
  Validation checks the record's shape; independently verify the manifest against the delivery.

`validate` checks the complete record against [`response-schema.json`](response-schema.json), using `jsonschema`, then checks checklist pins and verdict semantics. Stamp the response before final validation. The metadata is required for a completed assessment, even though the web app itself reads only the compact payload.

## The provenance stamp

`assessor` plus `object` plus `checklist_source` **is** the stamp, and every report repeats it in prose at its foot:

> Produced by `assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles` 0.1.0 with `stamped-conventions` 0.1.0, checklist 0.3.1 (`stamped-checklist-schema@v0.3.1`, `af259ba`), on <object url> at commit `<sha>`, 2026-10-13, <harness>/<model>.
> Probe output: `<path to the probe JSON>`.

When no commit exists, replace `at commit <sha>` with `at capture <uri>, SHA-256 <sha256>` in the prose stamp.

A report without the stamp cannot be compared against another iteration, so it is not finished.

## Report layout

Use this order, so the reader meets the actionable part first:

1. **Verdict line** — `MUST: n met / n partial / n unmet / n not-checked`, then SHOULD and MAY, each with its denominator.
   No single overall score, ever.
2. **What to fix first** — at most five, highest leverage first, each as *what to change* → *why it matters to this project* → *the item ids it closes*.
3. **What the project already does well** — two or three, with citations.
4. **Per-item table** — MUST first, then SHOULD, then MAY: id, principle codes, status, evidence, reason.
   `scripts/encode_response.py table <response>.json` renders exactly this from the response; it is not a table to type by hand.
5. **Flagged items** — every item carrying a `flags` entry, with one line each: what the probe measured versus what the item asks, or what the override was.
   An empty list is worth stating as "none".
6. **Not checked** — each with what would settle it.
7. **Goals and kind** — the project's stated goals (and where they came from: documentation, or the user's answers), its kind, and the emphasis that follows.
8. **The checklist URL**, the stamp, and a pointer to the response JSON.
   The URL is ~8–10 kB of base64 for a full 31-item response, so the report **links** `<date>-url.txt` rather than inlining it; a link a reader can click, not a wall they have to scroll.

Facts, from [stamped-checklist](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-checklist) at `d24d7ca`:

- The `responses` parameter is **standard base64** (not URL-safe) of UTF-8 JSON `{"checklist_version", "responses"}`, then percent-encoded as a query parameter.
- The app builds `?checklist=<v>&responses_version=<v>&cols=auto&sections=off&format=3&responses=<b64>` (`src/script.js`, `syncPersistentURL`).

# Verdict vocabulary

One status per checklist item, one reason, and evidence for anything other than `not-applicable`.
This reconciles @asmacdo's draft (pass/partial/fail/unknown), STAMPED-dl's met/partial/unmet/restricted/n-a, the [K-Dense #265](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/pull/265) review ("not checked with the tooling available" is not "unmet"), and the judgement statuses of [stamped-skills-assessment](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-skills-assessment).

| `status` | Use it when | App `value` | App `reason` holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `met` | Cited evidence shows the property holds across the object | `"yes"` | Not shown by the app; the citation lives in the response JSON |
| `partial` | It holds by design but is violated somewhere specific, or holds in some components only | `"no"` | Where it falls short, concretely |
| `unmet` | Evidence shows the property is absent | `"no"` | The shortest fix |
| `not-checked` | You could not check: tool missing, cost, access, or out of the agreed scope | `null` | Why, and what would settle it |
| `not-applicable` | The property cannot apply to this kind of object | `null` | `N/A: <reason>` |

## Rules

1. **A MUST item is never satisfied by `partial`.**
   Report `partial` and count it as a MUST failure.
2. **`not-checked` is reported separately from `unmet`, always.**
   Never fold it in, never score it as zero, and never let it disappear from a denominator: say `14/17 MUST met, 2 unmet, 1 not-checked`.
3. **`met` requires a citation** a reader can open: a path (with a line number where it helps), a commit, a run record, a URL, or a command with its output.
   "The project uses DataLad" is not evidence; `.datalad/config` at commit `abc1234` is.
4. **`unmet` requires evidence of absence**, not failure to find evidence.
   If you only failed to find it, that is `not-checked`.
5. **`not-applicable` is rare and argued**, and there are exactly two grounds for it:
   - **the kind of object** ([`project-kinds.md`](project-kinds.md)) — an object with no computation at all can be `not-applicable` on E.1; a dataset still has an environment for whatever produced it;
   - **an empty subject** — the thing the item asks about does not exist here.
     should/009 ("are restricted data or software kept in their own modules?") on an object whose every component is public has no subject: `met` would be a citation-free claim about a component that does not exist, and `unmet` would be false.

   Either way the reason names the ground, starting with `N/A:`.
   An item you merely could not check is `not-checked`, never this.
   After inspecting the complete delivery, use `not-applicable` for must/005 when no large binary data exists; apply the may/001 subject boundary below.

   **Not** an N/A ground: *there was nothing of this kind to do*.
   An object with no host assumptions to document satisfies must/011 — the requirement is "write down your assumptions", and having none meets it.
   Answer `met`, and let the reason carry the emptiness ("no host assumptions beyond a POSIX shell and the tracked lockfile; nothing undocumented remains").
   The difference from an empty subject is whether the *requirement* can be satisfied vacuously (must/011: yes) or the *property* has no instance to hold of (should/009 on an all-public object: no).

   **A declared process that has never run is `partial`**, not `met` and not `not-checked`.
   must/014 and should/008 ask for a process *and* for its updates to be tracked; a documented regeneration command with no update in the history is half of that, so say "declared in <file>, no instance in the history yet".
   **The commit that introduced the file is not an instance of updating it.**
   A lockfile committed once, with a regeneration command in its header, is "declared, never run": the creation is the declaration, not an instance of the process.
   **A declared process with instances in the history is `met`**: cite one.
   A blind run stalled on exactly this gap — a re-install step the history shows was carried out seventeen times fits neither "never run" nor "unmet" — so the three cases are: instances in the history → `met`; declared, no instance → `partial`; not declared → `unmet`.
   **The bar for "declared" is a command a reader could run**: `# pinned with uv pip compile code/requirements.in` in a lockfile header clears it; "dependencies are kept up to date" does not, and that is `unmet`.
   This is the commonest borderline case, and it comes up on every young object.
6. **`restricted`** (from STAMPED-dl) is **not a status here**.
   Restricted data that is properly isolated is `met` on should/009 and `not-checked` elsewhere with "access-restricted" as the reason.
7. **Equivalent evidence counts.**
   Name the mechanism you found rather than the tool you expected.
   Preserve the checklist pin; these are explicit property-based interpretations, not edits to its wording:
   - **must/003:** an installable package declaration in a delivered environment specification counts as inclusion; physical vendoring is not required. Judge completeness under must/010, exact environment identity under must/015, and archived artifacts under should/007; missing version pins alone do not show incompleteness.
   - **must/007:** discoverable installation and usage instructions can satisfy the item under another filename or in an equivalent delivered interface; `README.md` and `Makefile` are not mandatory names.
   - **may/001:** assess independently maintained project components, not ordinary runtime or package dependencies. No such components → `not-applicable`; otherwise require independently identified, retrievable links with clear boundaries, not necessarily Git submodules. An unidentified copy or unresolvable path fails. Judge missing or incomplete dependency environments under must/003 and must/010; they do not turn packages into project modules.
   - **must/006:** execution evidence must link the actual results and actions to their environment; a recognized provenance format or tool name alone is neither necessary nor sufficient.
   - **should/002, should/006:** inspect equivalent repeated-testing and environment-reconstitution records, including manual or scheduled runs; missing CI configuration alone proves neither property absent.
   Apply these interpretations consistently within a comparison and name any equivalent evidence used.
8. **Scripted before judged.**
   Run applicable probes and cite their output, then inspect evidence outside their supported representations.
   A tracked-path inventory, recognized filename or parsed DataLad record is not a complete delivered-artifact or provenance inventory.
   Missing probe support is `not-checked` pending inspection, not evidence of absence; record which probe or reading produced each verdict.
9. **Disagreements are surfaced, not averaged.**
   When a probe and a reading of the object disagree, report both and flag the item for the human.
10. **When the object tells two stories about how it runs, that disagreement *is* the answer.**
    An object can carry three accounts of its own execution — what the documentation says, what CI exercises, and what the run records recorded — and they need not agree.
    Judge **A.1 items (must/007, must/008, must/017) on the documented route**, because that is what a reader will follow; judge **T items on the records**, because that is what produced the results.
    Where the accounts disagree, the verdict is at most `partial`, the reason names both accounts, and the disagreement is reported as a finding in its own right: a README promising a container that the `Makefile` never invokes is worse than either an honest README or an honest Makefile.
    Four pairings and where each lands: documentation against the mechanism → **must/007, must/008, must/017**, and **should/002**, because a workflow tested against instructions nobody can follow is not tested; the mechanism against the run records → **must/006 and must/008** (what produced the results is not what is offered to reproduce them); CI against the records → **should/006** (the environment being tested is not the one the results came from); and the object's *metadata* against its own layout — a `dataset_description.json` naming a pipeline the history never ran — which has no checklist item and goes in `extra_items`.
    If naming both accounts will not fit in 250 characters, name the worse one in the reason and put the other in `evidence`; do not drop it.

    **An accurate disclosure is not a disagreement.**
    This rule exists for accounts that conflict *silently* — a README promising a container the `Makefile` never invokes.
    An object whose documentation states the difference and says which route produced the results is telling one story in two parts, and the items above stay `met` on it: the test is whether a reader following the documentation would be misled, not whether two routes exist.
    Two runs in a row marked a disclosed, accurate two-route object `partial` on four items under this rule; that is this rule being over-applied, and the reason to say so here.
    **The disclosure has to be true.**
    A comment in a CI workflow claiming it exercises the recorded environment, in a job whose steps never touch it, is not a disclosure: it is the silent conflict with an extra sentence, and it is worse than silence because it tells a reader not to check.
11. **A right answer reached by the wrong route is still a finding.**
    When a probe answers an item from a property the item does not ask about, the verdict may happen to be right and the reasoning is still wrong.
    Record it in the item's `flags` (`mapping-questioned`), say which property the probe actually measured, and keep your own verdict with `source` ending in `+judgement`.
    That is how a wrong probe-to-item mapping gets fixed instead of being inherited by every later report.

# Response, report and stamp

Every STAMPED assessment produces four files (five with the optional fresh-rerun report), named for **the day the assessment was made** (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DD`) — not the object's commit date, and not the date of an earlier assessment being redone:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `<date>-assessment.md` | the human report (layout below) |
| `<date>-response.json` | the machine-readable per-item answer, with evidence and pins |
| `<date>-probes.json` | what the scripted probes said, unedited, including the ones overridden |
| `<date>-url.txt` | the checklist-app URL, on one line |
| `<date>-fresh-rerun.json` | only when the expensive rerun probe was actually run |

The URL is derived from the response, never maintained by hand.
Two assessments of the same object on the same day get a `-2` suffix on all four; the second one's report says what changed and why.
Where the files are written is the calling skill's business; their names and shapes are this file's.

## Response JSON

A superset of the web app's persistence format 3.
The app ignores keys it does not know, so one file serves both.

```json
{
  "checklist_version": "0.3.1",
  "responses": {
    "stamped-checklist:must/009": {
      "value": "no",
      "reason": "code/plot.py line 12 opens an absolute path under a user home directory.",
      "status": "unmet",
      "evidence": [
        {"uri": "code/plot.py#L12", "description": "open(<absolute path under $HOME>)", "sha256": null}
      ],
      "source": "probe:no-abs-paths",
      "flags": []
    }
  },
  "schema_version": "0.2.0",
  "principles_version": "0.2.0",
  "checklist_source": {
    "repo": "https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-checklist-schema",
    "tag": "v0.3.1",
    "commit": "af259bad237fa57b856417db8dba45a1b283a527"
  },
  "extra_items": [
    {"key": "licence-declared", "status": "unmet", "reason": "No LICENSE, LICENSES/ or REUSE.toml; paper S.2/D.3 have no checklist item.", "evidence": []}
  ],
  "object": {"url": "…", "commit": "…", "captured_at": "2026-10-13T12:00:00Z", "kind": "study"},
  "assessor": {"skill": "assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles", "version": "0.2.0", "harness": "claude-code 2.1.x", "model": "…", "date": "2026-10-13",
               "dependencies": ["stamped-conventions@0.2.0"]},
  "scope": "Assessed the repository at the commit above; container images were not pulled."
}
```

- **Required core** (what the app reads): `checklist_version`, and `responses` with a `value` and a string `reason` per id — *in the payload the encoder builds*. The response JSON you write carries `status`, and `encode` derives `value` from it; `validate` therefore does not ask for a `value` and `set` does not write one. A `value` you write by hand that disagrees with its `status` is an error `validate` reports.
- Every one of the 31 pinned ids appears exactly once.
  A missing id is not "no answer"; it is a bug the validator catches.
- `status` is the richer verdict from [`verdicts.md`](verdicts.md); `value` is derived from it, never set by hand.
- **Cite a line only if you opened it.** `path#L12` is a promise that line 12 says what the reason claims; a run that cited line numbers it had not read then had to strip them all. Without that, cite the file (or `path#section`), which is still a citation a reader can follow.
- `evidence[]` uses stamped-skills-assessment's `Evidence` shape: `{uri, description, sha256?}`.
  `uri` is relative to the object's root, or absolute for anything outside it.
  **The argument lives here, not in `reason`.** 250 characters does not hold two cited accounts plus "the probe's heuristic said X but Y is true", and an override needs all three. Make `reason` the one-line verdict a reader sees in the app, and put each account, each command you ran and each number in an `evidence[]` entry with its own `description`.
- `source` is `probe:<name>`, `judgement`, or `probe:<name>+judgement` when a reading of the object overrode a probe (and then the item is flagged).
  Several probes may be named — `probe:entry-point+probe:ci-present+judgement` — which is what a verdict reached by **comparing two probes' evidence** looks like, and that comparison is itself the finding often enough to be worth recording.
- `flags[]` is optional and holds what a reader has to know about *how* the answer was reached, not what it says:
  - `mapping-questioned` — the probe answered this item from a property the item does not ask about ([`verdicts.md`](verdicts.md) rule 10);
  - `probe-overridden` — a reading of the object changed the probe's verdict;
  - `unverified-claim` — the verdict rests on something not confirmed independently, and the report says so;
  - `upstream-duplicate` — the checklist asks this question twice (must/014 and should/008 are the same sentence), so this answer repeats another by design rather than by mistake.

  Flagged items get their own short list in the report, after the per-item table.
  The list is **open**: these four are the ones in use, and a consumer that meets an unfamiliar flag shows it rather than dropping it.
- The `assessor` block may also carry `drafted_by` (the script or step that produced a draft, where that differs from the skill — `scripts/run_probes.py` sets it) and `note` (anything a reader needs about the assessor itself rather than about the object). Both are provenance *within* the assessor, not a second assessor.
- `extra_items[]` carries findings with no checklist id (licences, T.4) so they are reported without bending an existing id.
- `object.commit` names the inspected repository or preservation revision, not necessarily the worker's delivered state.
  Identify the original delivery snapshot/hash, capture omissions and stop-state evidence in `scope` and evidence citations; distinguish supplied resources and coordinator additions so they cannot earn worker credit. Keep the actual Git commit whenever one exists. For a delivery without a commit, set `object.commit` to `null` and supply `object.capture` with a retained manifest/archive's `uri` and SHA-256 `sha256`; never substitute the capture hash for a Git commit.
  The manifest must identify the delivered paths and content hashes plus capture omissions; an archive must contain the assessed bytes.
  Retain the referenced file so another assessor can verify the hash and boundary.
  Use `encode_response.py template -o <date>-response.json` when no Git probe draft is available, fill the assessment metadata and answers, then run `encode_response.py stamp <date>-response.json --capture <manifest-or-archive>` to hash the actual file.
  This preserves an existing commit; record the capture time in `object.captured_at` and the boundary in `scope`.
  Validation checks the record's shape; independently verify the manifest against the delivery.

`validate` checks the complete record against [`response-schema.json`](response-schema.json), using `jsonschema`, then checks checklist pins and verdict semantics. Stamp the response before final validation. The metadata is required for a completed assessment, even though the web app itself reads only the compact payload.

## The provenance stamp

`assessor` plus `object` plus `checklist_source` **is** the stamp, and every report repeats it in prose at its foot:

> Produced by `assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles` 0.1.0 with `stamped-conventions` 0.1.0, checklist 0.3.1 (`stamped-checklist-schema@v0.3.1`, `af259ba`), on <object url> at commit `<sha>`, 2026-10-13, <harness>/<model>.

A report without the stamp cannot be compared against another iteration, so it is not finished.

4. **`unmet` requires evidence of absence**, not failure to find evidence.
   If you only failed to find it, that is `not-checked`.
5. **`not-applicable` is rare and argued**, and there are exactly two grounds for it:
   - **the kind of object** ([`project-kinds.md`](project-kinds.md)) — an object with no computation at all can be `not-applicable` on E.1; a dataset still has an environment for whatever produced it;
   - **an empty subject** — the thing the item asks about does not exist here.
     should/009 ("are restricted data or software kept in their own modules?") on an object whose every component is public has no subject: `met` would be a citation-free claim about a component that does not exist, and `unmet` would be false.

   Either way the reason names the ground, starting with `N/A:`.
   An item you merely could not check is `not-checked`, never this.
   After inspecting the complete delivery, use `not-applicable` for must/005 when no large binary data exists; apply the may/001 subject boundary below.

   **Not** an N/A ground: *there was nothing of this kind to do*.
   An object with no host assumptions to document satisfies must/011 — the requirement is "write down your assumptions", and having none meets it.
   Answer `met`, and let the reason carry the emptiness ("no host assumptions beyond a POSIX shell and the tracked lockfile; nothing undocumented remains").
   The difference from an empty subject is whether the *requirement* can be satisfied vacuously (must/011: yes) or the *property* has no instance to hold of (should/009 on an all-public object: no).

   **A declared process that has never run is `partial`**, not `met` and not `not-checked`.
   must/014 and should/008 ask for a process *and* for its updates to be tracked; a documented regeneration command with no update in the history is half of that, so say "declared in <file>, no instance in the history yet".
   **The commit that introduced the file is not an instance of updating it.**
   A lockfile committed once, with a regeneration command in its header, is "declared, never run": the creation is the declaration, not an instance of the process.
   **A declared process with instances in the history is `met`**: cite one.
   A blind run stalled on exactly this gap — a re-install step the history shows was carried out seventeen times fits neither "never run" nor "unmet" — so the three cases are: instances in the history → `met`; declared, no instance → `partial`; not declared → `unmet`.
   **The bar for "declared" is a command a reader could run**: `# pinned with uv pip compile code/requirements.in` in a lockfile header clears it; "dependencies are kept up to date" does not, and that is `unmet`.
   This is the commonest borderline case, and it comes up on every young object.
6. **`restricted`** (from STAMPED-dl) is **not a status here**.
   Restricted data that is properly isolated is `met` on should/009 and `not-checked` elsewhere with "access-restricted" as the reason.
7. **Equivalent evidence counts.**
   Name the mechanism you found rather than the tool you expected.
   Preserve the checklist pin; these are explicit property-based interpretations, not edits to its wording:
   - **must/003:** an installable package declaration in a delivered environment specification counts as inclusion; physical vendoring is not required. Judge completeness under must/010, exact environment identity under must/015, and archived artifacts under should/007; missing version pins alone do not show incompleteness.
   - **must/007:** discoverable installation and usage instructions can satisfy the item under another filename or in an equivalent delivered interface; `README.md` and `Makefile` are not mandatory names.
   - **may/001:** assess independently maintained project components, not ordinary runtime or package dependencies. No such components → `not-applicable`; otherwise require independently identified, retrievable links with clear boundaries, not necessarily Git submodules. An unidentified copy or unresolvable path fails. Judge missing or incomplete dependency environments under must/003 and must/010; they do not turn packages into project modules.
   - **must/006:** execution evidence must link the actual results and actions to their environment; a recognized provenance format or tool name alone is neither necessary nor sufficient.
   - **should/002, should/006:** inspect equivalent repeated-testing and environment-reconstitution records, including manual or scheduled runs; missing CI configuration alone proves neither property absent.
   Apply these interpretations consistently within a comparison and name any equivalent evidence used.
8. **Scripted before judged.**
   Run applicable probes and cite their output, then inspect evidence outside their supported representations.
   A tracked-path inventory, recognized filename or parsed DataLad record is not a complete delivered-artifact or provenance inventory.
   Missing probe support is `not-checked` pending inspection, not evidence of absence; record which probe or reading produced each verdict.
9. **Disagreements are surfaced, not averaged.**
   When a probe and a reading of the object disagree, report both and flag the item for the human.
10. **When the object tells two stories about how it runs, that disagreement *is* the answer.**
    An object can carry three accounts of its own execution — what the documentation says, what CI exercises, and what the run records recorded — and they need not agree.
    Judge **A.1 items (must/007, must/008, must/017) on the documented route**, because that is what a reader will follow; judge **T items on the records**, because that is what produced the results.
    Where the accounts disagree, the verdict is at most `partial`, the reason names both accounts, and the disagreement is reported as a finding in its own right: a README promising a container that the `Makefile` never invokes is worse than either an honest README or an honest Makefile.
    Four pairings and where each lands: documentation against the mechanism → **must/007, must/008, must/017**, and **should/002**, because a workflow tested against instructions nobody can follow is not tested; the mechanism against the run records → **must/006 and must/008** (what produced the results is not what is offered to reproduce them); CI against the records → **should/006** (the environment being tested is not the one the results came from); and the object's *metadata* against its own layout — a `dataset_description.json` naming a pipeline the history never ran — which has no checklist item and goes in `extra_items`.
    If naming both accounts will not fit in 250 characters, name the worse one in the reason and put the other in `evidence`; do not drop it.

    **An accurate disclosure is not a disagreement.**
    This rule exists for accounts that conflict *silently* — a README promising a container the `Makefile` never invokes.
    An object whose documentation states the difference and says which route produced the results is telling one story in two parts, and the items above stay `met` on it: the test is whether a reader following the documentation would be misled, not whether two routes exist.
    Two runs in a row marked a disclosed, accurate two-route object `partial` on four items under this rule; that is this rule being over-applied, and the reason to say so here.
    **The disclosure has to be true.**
    A comment in a CI workflow claiming it exercises the recorded environment, in a job whose steps never touch it, is not a disclosure: it is the silent conflict with an extra sentence, and it is worse than silence because it tells a reader not to check.
11. **A right answer reached by the wrong route is still a finding.**
    When a probe answers an item from a property the item does not ask about, the verdict may happen to be right and the reasoning is still wrong.
    Record it in the item's `flags` (`mapping-questioned`), say which property the probe actually measured, and keep your own verdict with `source` ending in `+judgement`.
    That is how a wrong probe-to-item mapping gets fixed instead of being inherited by every later report.

## Mapping to the app

`scripts/encode_response.py` does this mapping; do not hand-roll it.
It also enforces the app's constraints: `value ∈ {"yes","no",null}`, `reason` a string of at most 250 characters, and every id known to the pinned checklist.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Yaroslav Halchenko <yaroslav.o.halchenko@dartmouth.edu>
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""STAMPED checklist responses: read the items, validate, encode, decode.

The vendored checklist in ``../checklist/`` is the only item source, and this
script is the only writer of a checklist-app URL.  See
``../references/response-format.md`` for the response JSON and
``../references/verdicts.md`` for the statuses.

Subcommands
-----------
items      list the pinned items (id, level, principle codes, text)
set        answer one item in a response JSON, in place (what every run was
           otherwise writing a merge script for)
table      the per-item markdown table response-format.md section 4 asks for
stamp      fill harness, model, scope and kind; optionally hash a retained capture
validate   check a response JSON against the pin and the app's constraints
encode     response JSON -> checklist-app URL
decode     checklist-app URL -> response JSON (how a filled web form becomes
           reference answers for calibration)
template   emit a response JSON skeleton with every item not-checked

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 validation failed, 2 usage.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import base64
import hashlib
import json
import pathlib
import sys
import urllib.parse

from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator, FormatChecker

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
CHECKLIST_DIR = HERE.parent / "checklist"
APP_URL = "https://checklist.stamped-principles.org/"
PERSISTENCE_FORMAT = 3
REASON_MAX = 250
# What `run_probes.py --response` writes for an item no probe covers. A finished
# response never still carries it: that is an unanswered item wearing the
# costume of an answer.
DRAFT_PLACEHOLDER = "No probe covers this item"

# status -> app value; see ../references/verdicts.md
STATUS_VALUE = {
    "met": "yes",
    "partial": "no",
    "unmet": "no",
    "not-checked": None,
    "not-applicable": None,
}
# A MUST item is never satisfied by `partial`.
MUST_SATISFYING = {"met"}


class Checklist:
    """The pinned items, read from the vendored JSON."""

    def __init__(self, path: pathlib.Path | None = None) -> None:
        self.lock = json.loads((CHECKLIST_DIR / "lock.json").read_text())
        self.path = path or CHECKLIST_DIR / self.lock["file"]
        data = json.loads(self.path.read_text())
        self.version = data["checklist_version"]
        self.schema_version = data.get("schema_version")
        self.principles_version = data.get("principles_version")
        self.items: list[dict] = []
        for level in data["data"]:
            for entry in level["entries"]:
                for item in entry["items"]:
                    self.items.append(
                        {
                            "id": item["id"],
                            "level": level["level"],
                            "principle_codes": list(entry["principle_codes"]),
                            "text": item["text"],
                        }

description: Assess how a project aligns with the STAMPED principles (self-contained, tracked, actionable, modular, portable, ephemeral, distributable) and leave a filled checklist behind — a dated report, a response JSON with per-item evidence, and a link that opens the answers in the STAMPED checklist app. Strictly read-only — it never changes the project it assesses. Use when asked to assess, audit, review or check a project, dataset or repository against STAMPED, to fill in the STAMPED checklist for something, or when another skill (align-, create-, do-full-research-loop) calls for an assessment.

user-invocable: true
